rules.title: Every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens

sources.text: **Everything visible is an asset** (`asset@1`). Engines compile assets into tokens/variables; UI reads only compiled tokens and never hardcodes colours or sizes. Hot-swap = `runtime.swap(type, id)`.

**All UI code conforms to the asset system (Oct 31 2026):** handwritten or generated, web CSS/TSX and Kotlin UI take every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border from asset tokens and use framework controls; `check-theme.mjs` + `check-controls.mjs` fail CI otherwise (file:line + token to use), `axf init` refuses non-conformant output, frozen Android code is held to `framework/spec/conform-baseline.json`.

**Handwritten code conforms to the hot-swappable asset system (Oct 31 2026, Brett):** handwritten code is allowed, but only if it conforms to the hot-swappable asset system. Anything the build system makes through the console (templates, boilerplates, the plugin generator, Build Pilot, orchestrator and headless builds) is not handwritten by default: it is generated from framework controls and assets. Conforms means every visual value comes from hot-swappable assets and their tokens: the theme (colours and style, `--fx-*`), the scale (typography, density and sizing, compact by default and big enough to tap on a phone), layout, component styles, and the menu, toolbar and dialog assets. Use the framework's controls instead of raw ones (web: `Button`, `fx-btn`, `fx-chip`, `fx-seg__opt`…; Kotlin: `AxfButton`, `AxfTextField`…). No hardcoded px, rem or em sizes, spacing, fonts, radii, border widths or colours, and no `var()` fallbacks. Kotlin takes them from `Axf.colors`, `Axf.type`, `Axf.space` and `Axf.shapes`. Test: swapping any asset must restyle the code with no edits. CI enforces it on all web CSS/TSX and Kotlin UI, handwritten or generated (`node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` in AmberX-AXF name file:line and the token to use; `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto tokens). The build engine refuses to finish `axf init` on output that doesn't conform. Only the framework's own token and asset definition files are exempt. Code that is frozen (Android on hold, Patches paused) is held to a baseline that can only shrink (`framework/spec/conform-baseline.json`).
**Everything visible is an asset** (`asset@1`). UI reads only engine-compiled tokens; never hardcode colours or sizes. Plugin and library UIs use theme tokens only (`framework/spec/THEMING.md`).

**Every toolbar is a Toolbars plugin toolbar (Nov 3 2026, Brett: "it really works on a computer"):** every existing and future toolbar, in every app, gets per-toolbar settings and the Toolbar editor through its context menu, accepts dropped hooks, and uses **tap-to-confirm on touch only**: on a finger tap the first tap shows what the button does and arms it (lit, 3 s by default, configurable), a second tap on it within the window runs it, a tap on another button re-arms that one; mouse, trackpad, pen and keyboard stay a single click with the usual hover tooltip, decided per interaction (a touchscreen laptop: finger = double tap, mouse = single click). rules.title: Plugin and library UIs use framework controls and theme tokens only

sources.text: **Plugin and library UIs conform to the theme engines** (tokens only, framework layout primitives, `axf-<lib>` / `axp-<plugin>` naming, never define `--fx-*`); a plugin wanting its own look ships its own assets through the engines (scoping not built yet). The future plugin designer depends on this. Spec: `framework/spec/THEMING.md`. CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).

**Plugins inherit the app's style (Oct 22 2026, Brett):** every plugin UI conforms to the style theme engine, so a plugin looks like the app it runs in: if the app changes its button style (button asset, style theme, spacing), every plugin's buttons change with it, and the same for every other control (sliders, switches, fields, containers, dialogs, menus, tabs). Plugins build controls only from the framework's components (`Button`, `Switch`, `TextField`, `SelectField`, `Container`, …) or its engine-styled classes (`fx-btn`, `fx-iconbtn`, …), never their own styled buttons or controls; a plugin's CSS may lay things out but never restyles a control. Same for libraries and every app on the framework.

They can't drift any more: every build of every profile is one record in the builds store (`_claude/builds/store.json`, builds@1, owned by the orchestrator), and the orchestrator view, the Pending builds list (steps as `[Fable]`/`[Opus]` sub prompts), the build queue and the Build manager are projections of it. rules.title: Veto calls: send once with a reason and keep building

sources.text: **It's a veto system, not approvals (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "It's not an approval system anymore. It's a veto system. … You send the notice that you're going to be making changes, and then my VPS waits three minutes before sending it unless I click deny … you don't stop, you just build and you don't check for its completion."; axHub decision #103):** every axHub call that needs Brett (VPS commands, GitHub writes, PRs, merges, deletes on the hub, any MCP tool) is a **veto call**: axHub holds it, pushes the notice through the AmberX app, and Vinnie runs it after the countdown (**90 seconds** since Oct 30 2026, axHub decision #104) unless he taps **Deny**. He can also tap **Approve** (runs it at once) or **Shelve** (pauses the countdown until he approves or denies it); a session never does any of these for him and can't (the hub takes them only from his signed-in session). Send it **once** with its `reason`, tell Brett in one line what is coming (the Deny link is optional, never "approve"), and **keep building**: don't wait for the countdown, don't poll, don't re-send, don't schedule checks for its completion, don't ask him to approve anything. Read the job with `get_job` only when a later step truly needs its output, and only once. A denied call stays denied unless he asks again. (Replaces "Send approvals once, never poll" #101, "Approvals" Oct 20 with its retry timing, and "Veto calls are sent once" Oct 28.)

rules.title: Every change reaches main through a PR up to date with main

sources.text: **Automatic merge (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "When stuff needs to merge automatic merge"; replaces "Ready to merge = send him a merge approval", Oct 27):** PRs merge by themselves. The console's push banner auto-merges every open PR in the watched repos (AmberX-AXF, axHub, Build-Pilot by default) that is ready: not a draft, no conflicts, CI passed on its head commit (pinned) — every 3 minutes, no Claude session, no tokens (setting *Auto-merge* in Settings → Plugins → Push banner, on by default). So a session just opens the PR (`github.pulls/create` or the push banner's Open PR, a veto call) and moves on: no merge call, no asking, no checking. A repo without CI never gets a green result and never auto-merges, so every watched repo has CI (axHub: `.github/workflows/test.yml`, `pnpm test`, since Oct 30 2026). **Every change through a PR, up to date with main (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "I want everything to need a PR and to pull against main before it's merged"):** (one exception since Nov 3 2026, Brett: build status goes live — in AmberX-AXF the builds store's status-only commits from `framework/cli/builds-live.mjs` go straight to main, `_claude/` data only, never code) nothing reaches main except through a pull request — no direct pushes or merges to main, from any session, script or workflow (bots push to their own branch). The push banner (0.5.0) opens a PR for every branch ahead of main (setting *Open a pull request for every branch*, on by default), takes ready PRs oldest first, pulls main into one that is behind (head pinned) and merges it only once it is 0 behind and CI passed on that new head; at most one merge per round, so the next PR is brought up to date with the new main and re-tested first. rules.title: The build pipeline: Pending → Queue → Building, started only by the dispatcher

sources.text: **The build pipeline: Pending → Queue → Building (Nov 8 2026, Brett: "what I say, send a build to the orchestrator … he sends everything to the pending. And I have to send them from pending to queue"; build `urgent-rebuild-pipeline-orchestrator-ids-splits-`):** every request becomes a build in the orchestrator (the store assigns the id); a build with no steps is split by the orchestrator itself (`pipeline.mjs intake`: one Opus call, ≤ 30-min steps, Fable only where needed; hand-written steps are never re-split unless *Split now* asks) and sits in **Pending**. Only Brett moves a build to the **Queue** (Pipeline tab → Queue, `pipeline.mjs queue <id>`, MCP / voice `pipeline-queue`; *Launch builds without asking* ON queues split builds by itself). No session, agent or script starts a Queue build by hand: the **dispatcher** (`apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/pipeline.mjs tick`, cron `axf-pipeline` every minute) starts the next Queue build only when an agent slot and a Claude account that runs its next phase's model are free (Fable phases to accounts with Fable, Opus work to the others first), through `deploy/claude-headless.sh --account`. A session that stops with steps left goes back to the Queue (phase done, or a crash, 3 runs at most) or to Pending for Brett; nothing running while the Queue has work raises one phone alert. `queued` is a builds@1 status; the record is build-pipeline@1 (`framework/core/build-pipeline.mjs`). <!-- axf-plugin:build-orchestrator -->
